summary: Statistics Norway has published child victims of reported sexual offences and maltreatment by immigrant background (with a Europe / outside-Europe split and rates per 1,000), charges by immigrant background and country group, and child-welfare measures every year by immigrant category. All are birth-country proxies, not ethnicity, and the third generation counts as 'rest of the population'.

nations.National (SSB, Kripos, KOM): SSB articles and Statbank tables by immigrant background; Kripos homicide overview; KOM trafficking reports.

european_title: Not recorded by any Norwegian source
european_note: Norwegian statistics record immigrant background from the birth country of the person, parents and grandparents, never ethnicity. The 'rest of the population' plus immigrants and their children from Europe is the closest to European descent, but it is a proxy: the rest of the population includes the grandchildren of immigrants from anywhere and people with one foreign-born parent, and 'Europe' is a birth-country region, not descent. SSB's country groups put non-EU Europe (for example Ukraine, Russia and the Balkans) with Africa and Asia.

proxy_note: Norway records immigrant background (birth country of the person, parents and grandparents) and citizenship, never ethnicity. Every group below is a proxy, not ethnicity.

harms.label: Rape of a child under 14 (reported to police)
harms.intro: An average of 692 victims a year were recorded for reported rape of a child under 14 in 2017-2022, and 517 for sexual acts with a child under 16. SSB published these by immigrant background, with the background split into Europe and outside Europe and rates per 1,000 by age. A second SSB article gives charges for the same offences by immigrant background and country group for 2020-2023. Both are one-off articles, not annual tables.

victims.scope: Norway, victims of reported rape of a child under 14, annual average 2017-2022
victims.share_note: SSB article 'Innvandrere oftere utsatt for vold og bedrageri', Table 6: victims of offences reported to the police, annual average 2017-2022. Counts as published (annual averages are rounded separately, so Europe and outside-Europe may not add exactly to the total); shares calculated here; the remainder are victims who are not registered residents or have no background recorded. Counts: rest of population 591, immigrants 44 (Europe 13, outside Europe 31), Norwegian-born with immigrant parents 46 (Europe 12, outside Europe 34). Immigrant background (SSB): immigrants were born abroad to two foreign-born parents and four foreign-born grandparents; Norwegian-born with immigrant parents were born in Norway to two immigrant parents. Everyone else is the 'rest of the population' (øvrig befolkning): Norwegian-born to Norwegian-born parents, but also people with one foreign-born parent, people born abroad to Norwegian-born parents and the grandchildren of immigrants. 'Europe' and 'outside Europe' refer to the immigrant's (or the parents') country of birth. This is a birth-country proxy, not ethnicity.

Country group 1 is the Nordic countries, EU/EFTA, the UK, North America and Oceania; group 2 is Europe outside EU/EFTA and the UK, Africa, Asia and Latin America. Birth-country proxy, not ethnicity.

harms.label: Child-welfare care measures (Statbank)
harms.intro: 6,324 children aged 0-17 had a child-welfare care measure (omsorgstiltak) on 31 December 2025. Statbank publishes them every year by immigrant category and country group with rates per 1,000. Care measures follow neglect, abuse and other serious failures of care; they are not neglect alone. No perpetrator data.

victims.scope: Norway, children 0-17 with a care measure on 31 December 2025
victims.rate_label: children per 1,000 of the same group had a care measure on 31 December 2025
victims.share_note: Shares calculated here from the Statbank counts; rates as published. Statbank table 11298. 'Without immigrant background' is SSB's 'barn og unge elles' (everyone who is not an immigrant or Norwegian-born to immigrant parents, including the third generation and children with one foreign-born parent). Group 1 countries: the Nordic countries, EU/EFTA, the UK, USA, Canada, Australia and New Zealand; group 2: all other countries, including Europe outside EU/EFTA and the UK. Birth-country proxy, not ethnicity.

perpetrators.text: Child-welfare statistics do not record who caused the harm.

harms.label: Homicide (Kripos national overview)
harms.intro: Kripos recorded 19 homicide victims and 23 perpetrators in 2025; 2 victims were children. It publishes both by citizenship and says which Norwegian citizens were born abroad, for all ages; the child victims are not given by citizenship. SSB gives 379 charges for homicide (incl. attempts) in 2020-2023 by immigrant background and country group.

harms.label: Trafficking in human beings
harms.intro: There is no national count of trafficking victims by nationality. The coordinating unit KOM (National Police Directorate) reports about 200 presumed victims receiving assistance each year in 2022-2024, many of them foreign citizens, and 8 minors placed by child welfare in 2024 under suspicion of trafficking, all boys aged 13-16 from Asian countries. SSB's victim tables count an average of 38 victims of reported trafficking a year (2017-2022), but the background split is mostly suppressed.

victims.share_note: KOM report 2024: 'all were from Asian countries'. Country of origin, a proxy, not ethnicity. Tiny, selected group.

breakdown.why: SSB gives victims of reported sexual offences against children (rape of a child under 14, sexual acts with a child under 16) by immigrant background and age with rates per 1,000 (annual average 2017-2022), and charges for the same offences by immigrant background and country-group (2020-2023). Both are one-off SSB articles; charges not persons; no linkage.

SSB gives child victims of reported maltreatment in close relations by immigrant background and age with rates per 1,000 (2017-2022) and charges for maltreatment in close relations by immigrant background and country-group (2020-2023).

Statbank table 11298 gives children with child-welfare care measures in 2025 by immigrant category and country-group with rates per 1,000 (no immigrant background 5.8; immigrants 6.6; Norwegian-born to immigrant parents 5.2). Care measures are not only neglect; no perpetrator data.

Kripos's national homicide overview 2025 gives the 19 victims and 23 perpetrators by citizenship and whether Norwegian citizens were born abroad, all ages; SSB gives homicide charges by immigrant background. The 2 child victims in 2025 are not given by citizenship.

No national count of trafficking victims by nationality: KOM's 2024 report says the 8 minors placed by child welfare were all from Asian countries; SSB victim counts by background are mostly suppressed. No trafficker data.

Only 'sexually offensive behaviour towards a child under 16' (which includes, but does not separate, online offences) by immigrant background, for victims and charges. No abuse-material figures by background.

components.name: Victim heritage
components.full: Official data by harm that separately identify children of European descent (e.g. White non-Hispanic, White British) alongside every other group, self-reported or official, few unknowns. Broad categories that lump European-descent people with others get partial credit; proxies (nationality, citizenship, migration background, country of birth) at most 9.4 points.

components.name: Perpetrator heritage
components.full: Same standard for perpetrators: not perceived, few unknowns, European descent separately identified. Proxies at most 9.4 points.

components.name: Coverage and missing data
components.full: Over 90% of the population covered, under 10% unknown

components.name: Rates and linkage
components.full: Rates per 100,000 possible, and victim heritage linked to perpetrator heritage

score.gold_standard: 100% means a country publishes data that separately identifies people of European descent, both as perpetrators (so one can tell when they disproportionately harm a group) and as child victims (so one can tell when European-descent children are disproportionately harmed), alongside every other group, linked victim to perpetrator, for every harm.
score.rules: Heritage is 75 of every 100 points (victims 37.5, perpetrators 37.5); coverage, rates and access share the other 25. Proxies such as nationality or migration background earn at most a quarter of the heritage points. A country with no real ethnicity data for victims or perpetrators is capped at 25%.
score.why: Norway scores 22% on the stricter scale (20-40%). Statistics Norway has published child victims of reported sexual offences and maltreatment by immigrant background with rates per 1,000, charges by immigrant background and country-group, and annual child-welfare measures by immigrant category. These are birth-country proxies from one-off articles, and the third generation is counted in the 'rest of the population'.
score.weights_id: harm weights of 19 Nov 2026 (homicide 25, sexual abuse 20, sex trafficking 20, physical abuse 15, online exploitation 10, neglect 10)
